new.title: Large Language Models explained briefly
new.summary: Grant Sanderson visually explains next-token prediction, model parameters, pretraining, human-feedback tuning and the transformer attention mechanism. The lesson shows how language models produce fluent output without independently checking facts. A detailed companion lesson supports these concepts; this is an evergreen explanation, not a current product launch or October 2026 news clip.
new.why_it_matters: Use the explanation to distinguish fluent text generation from reliable evidence. Ask how an answer was grounded and checked instead of treating confident or plausible wording as proof of correctness.
practical_takeaways: LLMs repeatedly predict token probabilities from context
Pretraining and human-feedback tuning serve different objectives
Transformers refine contextual representations through attention

old.title: VideoGen Model 1 launch film

The page also distinguishes the launch film from longer generated examples. This is useful as a compact product orientation; claims and examples remain publisher-controlled. The page and text were reviewed, but playback was not performed.
old.why_it_matters: Use the clip and page to define a pilot brief, then compare narrative consistency, correction effort, provenance and cost across several prompts instead of treating one launch montage as performance evidence.

new.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Prompt Engineering: Optimizing AI Models
new.summary: Martin Keen compares three ways to improve AI responses: clearer prompting, retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning. The lesson distinguishes situations needing up-to-date or proprietary facts from those needing better instructions or more specialized model behavior. It explains the different infrastructure, latency and training implications; this is an evergreen methods lesson, not an independent vendor benchmark.
new.why_it_matters: Diagnose the failure before selecting a tool. Start with clearer instructions, retrieve trusted current documents when knowledge is missing, and only consider fine-tuning when a measured specialization problem justifies its training cost.
practical_takeaways: Prompt engineering changes instructions without altering model weights
RAG retrieves external current evidence into generation context
Fine-tuning adjusts model parameters and demands suitable training data
new.duration_fallback_reason: 13:10 covers three technical alternatives and their trade-offs in useful depth; the prior sub-two-minute product demo failed reader value.

old.title: Keep Your Glean Skills Up to Date with Skill Reflection
old.summary: Glean’s original product-video page identifies a short Skill Reflection demonstration; its companion product article explains that accumulated feedback becomes a proposed skill update which a user must approve. An independent index reports a 1:36 runtime. The material offers a concrete governance pattern for maintaining reusable procedures. Page content was reviewed, but playback was not performed.
old.why_it_matters: Use the demonstration as a review pattern: collect repeated corrections, inspect the supporting feedback and approve only durable changes, keeping one-off project preferences out of a shared skill.

new.title: Is Education Failing our Students in this AI-Driven World?
new.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson discuss how pervasive AI changes the foundational knowledge students need, how personalized learning might work, and why schools struggle to adapt. They explore opportunities for educators while preserving critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving skills. The publisher's episode-specific transcript establishes that AI, rather than general world news, is the sustained subject. Audio playback was not performed.
new.why_it_matters: Apply the discussion to professional AI education: teach verification, judgment and problem framing alongside tool proficiency. Pilot AI-supported learning with human oversight, and measure learner understanding rather than merely completed assignments.
new.editorial_ai_fraction_review: predominant based on whole episode transcript; exact percentage unmeasured; user-quality criterion recommended >=75%
practical_takeaways: AI changes which literacy and reasoning skills deserve classroom time
Personalized tools need teacher oversight and critical-thinking safeguards
Institutional incentives and teacher authority constrain education reform
